LESSON: SIGN READING 11.2.2 COMPREHENSION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.2: Sign Reading 11.2.2 Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 11.2.2 Comprehension, part of Strand 11 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three General.

Key inquiry question: How do we predict what will happen in a story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 11.2.2 Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: as the learner responds to comprehension questions.

• Creativity and imagination: as the learner makes predictions of what will happen in the story.

Values:
Responsibility: as learner takes initiative to get clues from the story read to answer indirect questions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Environmental and Social Issues: the learner gains and uses information about safety during playtime and games.

Link to other Learning Areas

Comprehension skills are applicable while reasing texts in all other learning areas.

Suggested Learning Resources

Chart, Class readers, Adapted Course books, Flash cards, Recording devices e.g tablets, mobile phone, Dictionary, Internet, Audio-visual recordings,

Posters, Pictures and Photographs, Extracts from newspapers, magazines.
